note: The strongest training-free system on this benchmark (69.3% dev, 72.28% test, 69.36% R-VES) and the one this repository has cited most: the SQL-Like intermediate language, the result-set equality vote and the self-taught CoT triples are all ported here, and `benchmarks.md` names it twenty times. It was nevertheless absent from this file until round 151 — which meant `intakeGaps` could not report it, so `released and unpinned` never listed it and 'copy it in pieces rather than dispatch it' was a paragraph no machine had read. The two obstacles are real and are stated here so a dispatch can be argued against them: value retrieval is an HNSW index over cells and column names, which needs an embedding backend this repository currently cannot reach, and its 69.3% was measured on GPT-4o, so a same-endpoint comparison has to be re-run on `deepseek-chat` and will not be that number.

Pinned and dispatched. Paired on the same 498 questions and the same endpoint it beat the adopted arm by 4.84pp (p = 0.0160) while the four component readings summed to less than that gap, which is the whole argument for copying a pipeline instead of pricing its levers one at a time.
Pinned. Five agents, ten candidates drawn twice, unit tests generated and evaluated: the run needs an embedding model and a few hundred calls, so it is dispatched rather than run per push.

The README's roadmap lists the four withheld modules as future releases, and `ScaleSQL/modules` holds only the schema side, so the repository is the preprocessing half of an 81.67% test run. Running it produces a schema, not a system: the number it would make belongs to a hybrid and may not be plotted as theirs. Also the first leader in this queue whose gain is largely a 32B fine-tune plus vLLM, which this repository cannot host behind an API.

No release exists, re-checked on 2026-11-16 three ways: the arXiv page carries no artifact or code link in its abstract, body or appendix and names sqlglot, datasketch, kshingle and FAISS only as dependencies; a repository search for the name returns 161 items that are unrelated commercial products; and the single repository whose description names the method is a stub with one directory and no README. What the paper does carry is enough to write code, and that is now the case: `eval/bird/askdata.ts` rebuilds section 3 -- the shingle index over up to 10,000 distinct values per field, the five schema variants with the union of the fields their statements read, and step 2.d with `MaxRetry` as a parameter because the paper does not state its value -- and `askdata-shape` is the arm that carries it, one lever from `select-mixed-rule` at eight calls a case against three. Four of the five mechanisms were already priced here (profile summary +3.6pp, three candidates, vote which lost 2.74pp to `shortest`, corrections bounded at 0.4pp); the open one was the linker, whose own ablation puts it at +1.8pp against +6.2pp for perfect linking. One community rebuild of the four-stage pipeline reports 95.6% mean column recall and 90.5% F1 in linking but 61.8% BIRD accuracy against the paper's 76.14-78.49 dev, which is what a rebuild of the published part buys when the unpublished part is the prompt text and the eight retrieved examples. No number from the arm may be filed under this row: a rebuild's first reading is a number with no denominator.

mechanisms: m-schema semi-structured card with types primary keys and example values
icl examples chosen by named-entity overlap rather than by embedding distance
refiner that repairs logic or syntax per candidate
fine-tuned selection model instead of self-consistency
note: Read on 2026-11-22: the repository holds seven files, of which five are images, a licence and two READMEs. There is no pipeline code, and the README's own timeline still lists the complete code as unreleased, so the only runnable artifacts are M-Schema and the weights. A 32B generator and a fine-tuned selector need a GPU, which a GitHub runner does not have, so `partial` is not modesty here: the half that carries the score cannot start on the machine this repository dispatches to. Its ablation is the useful part and it is already printed in `benchmarks.md`: one generator costs 4.04pp, majority vote instead of the selector costs 3.13pp, no schema filter costs 1.24pp. Two numbers of theirs were mislabelled in this document until this round: 75.63 is the **test** score, dev is **73.34**; the gap to it is 7.41pp, not 9.7.

mechanisms: complexity-aware routing by one llm judger call per question
dag decomposition into atomic sub-questions each answered by its own generation
rag over semantically similar training examples grounding the decomposer
topology refiner that rebuilds the plan when execution fails
schema selector pruning the card before generation
note: BIRD **dev** 1,534 questions, 70.53%, backbone DeepSeek-V3 (`deepseek-chat`) at temperature 0 for the judger and the direct path, 0.1 for the decomposer. The backbone is the argument this entry exists for: the same API name this repository calls, so 'it scores higher because its model is stronger' is not available as an explanation for these 4.6pp. Its own ablation (770-question subset, full pipeline 69.48) prices four of the five components: always decompose -10.65pp, no decomposition -1.43pp, no topology refinement -0.78pp, no schema selector -1.82pp (tokens x6.3). The component it never ablates is the rag examples, which is the only one that adds knowledge rather than procedure. No artifact of any kind is published, and the leaderboard's model-availability column is empty, so this is a rebuild with the paper as its only checklist. A row named GenaSQL on the 2026-10-29 leaderboard snapshot carries exactly 70.53 dev / 72.28 test; whether it is the same submission under a team name is unverified and is not assumed here.
